docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page describes the internal architecture of the agent-foundry CLI and repository.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
agent-foundry is a Python CLI that installs registry-defined plugins into Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor IDE, and Cursor CLI.

Plugins live under plugins/ and are indexed in registry/plugins.yaml. End users install bundles; this repository also contains the CLI implementation and validation logic.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
registry/plugins.yaml  →  RegistryRepository
                              ↓
plugins/<id>/          →  validate-plugins (ManifestConsistency, BundleStructure)
                              ↓
agent_foundry/installers/*_provider.py  →  install-plugin / install / uninstall

docs.title: Repository: validate-plugins
docs.text:
The validate-plugins command checks registry and manifest consistency before install:

  1. Load registry/plugins.yaml via RegistryRepository
  2. For each plugin under plugins/<id>/, run validation rules:
  3. ManifestConsistency — manifest name/version must match registry
  4. BundleStructure — required directories and files exist
  5. Skill/agent frontmatter checks
  6. Exit non-zero on any failure

Run from the repository root after changing plugins or the registry.

docs.title: Install: install-plugin / install
docs.text:
Install commands resolve the source repository, locate plugin or item content, and delegate to a provider-specific installer:

  1. Resolve source — default GitHub fetch, --repo override, or local discovery
  2. Locate content — registry lookup or external repo layout (agents/, skills/, plugins/)
  3. Apply path overrides — optional --path <kind>:<dir> for non-standard layouts
  4. Provider install — copy or symlink files to provider-specific discovery paths
  5. Track state — record install destinations for uninstall (under .agent-foundry/)

Uninstall reverses tracked destinations; it does not require --path.

docs.title: Repository map
docs.text:
Path Purpose agent_foundry/ CLI entrypoint, registry loading, per-provider installers, plugin validation and scaffolding plugins/ Distributable plugin bundles (skills, agents, commands, MCP configs) registry/plugins.yaml Central plugin index (id, path, version, summary) tests/ Unit tests (unittest) scripts/e2e-cli.sh, e2e.md Optional manual end-to-end smoke tests pyproject.toml Package metadata and agent-foundry console script docs/ MkDocs documentation site (this site)

Do not treat build/, *.egg-info/, or local install state under ~/.agent-foundry/ as source of truth.

docs.title: Key modules
docs.text: Module Responsibility agent_foundry/cli/app.py argparse wiring; subcommands: install-plugin, install, uninstall, validate-plugins, create-plugin, remove-plugin agent_foundry/registry/ Loads and parses registry/plugins.yaml; external repo layout in external.py agent_foundry/installers/ One module per provider (cursor_provider.py, cursor_cli_provider.py, claude_provider.py, codex_provider.py, copilot_provider.py); shared selection and source-path logic agent_foundry/plugin/validation/rules.py Duplicate plugin ids; manifest consistency; bundle structure; skill/agent frontmatter agent_foundry/plugin/crud/ create-plugin scaffold, remove-plugin

docs.title: Cursor CLI install behavior
docs.text: Cursor CLI install mirrors plugin skills to .cursor/skills/<name>/ and agents to .cursor/agents/, with state under .agent-foundry/cursor-cli/.

docs.title: Setup and validation commands
docs.text:
Run from the repository root after changes:

pip install -e .
agent-foundry --help
agent-foundry validate-plugins
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
pip install vulture
vulture agent_foundry tests --min-confidence 100

Optional: scripts/e2e-cli.sh (see e2e.md).

CI runs the same checks in .github/workflows/agent-foundry-ci.yml. The aggregate job required-checks must pass before merge.

docs.title: Implementation guidelines
docs.text:
1. Minimal diffs — match naming, structure, and style of surrounding code
  2. Plugin ids — lowercase kebab-case only; prefer agent-foundry create-plugin <id>
  3. Registry edits — after changing plugins/ or registry/plugins.yaml, run validate-plugins
  4. CLI/installer changes — add or update tests under tests/ (use unittest, not pytest)
  5. Dead code — CI runs vulture at confidence 100
  6. Secrets — never commit credentials, tokens, or .env files

docs.title: Providers quick reference
docs.text:
Supported provider values: claude, codex, copilot, cursor, cursor-cli.

Install kinds for granular install: agent, skill, mcp-config. Identifiers may use plugin_id:resource when ambiguous.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Thanks for helping improve agent-foundry — the CLI for installing registry-defined plugins into Codex, Claude Code, Cursor (IDE and CLI), and Copilot CLI.

Full documentation is published at josemiguelmelo.github.io/agent-foundry.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Requirements: Python 3.10+

From the repository root:

pip install -e .
agent-foundry --help

Optional: install pipx to exercise the published install path (pipx install -e .).

docs.title: AI-assisted development
docs.text:
If you use Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or other coding agents on this repo:

  • AGENTS.md — canonical project context (architecture, commands, boundaries)
  • .cursor/rules/ — Cursor rules (always-on + path-scoped)
  • .github/copilot-instructions.md and .github/instructions/ — Copilot repo-wide and path-specific rules
  • CLAUDE.md — imports AGENTS.md for Claude Code

Update AGENTS.md when conventions change; keep tool-specific files short and pointing to it.

docs.title: What to contribute
docs.text: Area Location Notes Registry plugins plugins/, registry/plugins.yaml Skills, agents, commands, MCP configs for end users CLI and installers agent_foundry/ Provider adapters, install/uninstall logic, validation Tests tests/ Unit tests; add coverage for new behavior Docs docs/, README.md, plugin READMEs Keep usage examples in sync with the CLI

docs.title: Adding or updating a plugin
docs.text:
1. Scaffold (recommended for new plugins):
agent-foundry create-plugin <plugin_id> --version 0.1.0 --summary "Short description"

Plugin ids must be lowercase kebab-case (e.g. my-workflow).

  1. Edit the generated tree under plugins/<plugin_id>/:
  2. Skills: skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
  3. Agents: agents/<agent-name>.md
  4. Commands: commands/<command-name>.md (where supported)

  5. Provider manifests: .cursor-plugin/, .claude-plugin/, .codex-plugin/, plugin.json, etc.

  6. Register the plugin in registry/plugins.yaml if create-plugin did not already add an entry (it usually does).

  7. Validate before opening a PR:

agent-foundry validate-plugins
  1. Remove a plugin from the registry (does not uninstall from user machines):
agent-foundry remove-plugin <plugin_id>

See Plugin development and existing plugins such as plugins/git/ for layout patterns.

docs.title: Working on the CLI
docs.text:
• Entry point: agent_foundry/cli/app.py
  • Run the full unit suite:
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
  • Dead-code check (CI enforces this):
pip install vulture
vulture agent_foundry tests --min-confidence 100
  • Optional end-to-end smoke: scripts/e2e-cli.sh (see e2e.md)

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
Preview the docs locally:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve

Build with strict link checking:

mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
1. Branch from main using a clear prefix, e.g. docs/add-contributing, feat/my-feature, fix/issue-description.
  2. Keep changes focused; one logical concern per PR when possible.
  3. Fill out .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md — especially plugin/registry impact and validation checkboxes.
  4. Ensure CI passes:
  5. agent-foundry validate-plugins
  6. Unit tests
  7. vulture dead-code scan
  8. Required aggregate check required-checks

Describe what changed and why in the PR summary. Note any security or operational risk if you touch hooks, commands, or MCP server definitions.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Use Conventional Commits style when practical:

  • feat: new behavior
  • fix: bug fix
  • docs: documentation only
  • refactor:, test:, chore:, ci: as appropriate

Example: docs: add CONTRIBUTING guide for plugins and PR workflow

docs.title: Plugin Development
docs.text: This guide covers how to create and maintain registry plugins under plugins/.

docs.title: Plugin layout
docs.text:
Each registry plugin typically includes:

  • .agentic/plugin.yaml — name, version, description (must match registry entry)
  • plugin.json and provider dirs: .cursor-plugin/, .claude-plugin/, .codex-plugin/
  • skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md — YAML frontmatter + markdown body
  • agents/<agent-name>.md — YAML frontmatter + role/guidelines
  • commands/<name>.md — where supported by providers
  • .mcp.json — optional MCP server definitions

Example reference: plugins/git/.

docs.title: Scaffold a new plugin
docs.text:
agent-foundry create-plugin <plugin_id> --version 0.1.0 --summary "Short description"

Plugin ids must be lowercase kebab-case only (e.g. my-workflow).

The command creates the directory tree under plugins/<plugin_id>/ and appends an entry to registry/plugins.yaml.

docs.title: Registry entry
docs.text:
Each plugin is indexed in registry/plugins.yaml:

plugins:
  - id: my-plugin
    path: plugins/my-plugin
    version: 0.1.0
    summary: Short description shown in the catalog

Manifest name and version in .agentic/plugin.yaml and provider manifests must match the registry entry. CI validates this with validate-plugins.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Skills live in skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md:

skills/
  my-skill/
    SKILL.md

Each SKILL.md file uses YAML frontmatter followed by markdown instructions.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Agents are single markdown files in agents/:

agents/
  my-agent.md

Each file uses YAML frontmatter with role and guidelines.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Commands are supported on some providers:

commands/
  my-command.md

docs.title: Provider manifests
docs.text:
Each plugin includes provider-specific manifest files so the CLI knows how to install content:

Provider Manifest location Cursor .cursor-plugin/plugin.json Claude Code .claude-plugin/plugin.json OpenAI Codex .codex-plugin/plugin.json GitHub Copilot CLI plugin.json Registry / CI .agentic/plugin.yaml

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Always validate before opening a PR:

agent-foundry validate-plugins

Validation checks:

  • Duplicate plugin ids
  • Manifest name/version consistency with registry
  • Bundle structure (required directories and files)
  • Skill and agent frontmatter

docs.title: Remove a plugin
docs.text:
agent-foundry remove-plugin <plugin_id>

This deletes plugins/<plugin_id>/ and its registry entry in this repository only. It does not uninstall from user machines.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• plugins/ are end-user products — do not confuse them with repo dev instructions (AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules/).
  • Provider behavior — when changing install paths or scope (--global vs --in-project), update docs and add tests.
  • Do not modify generated artifacts (build/, agent_foundry.egg-info/) unless fixing packaging intentionally.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: agent-foundry uses release-please to automate version bumps, changelog updates, tags, and GitHub Releases.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Merge feature and fix PRs to main with Conventional Commit titles.
  2. The release-please workflow runs on each push to main.
  3. release-please opens or updates a Release PR (for example, chore(main): release 1.1.0) that bumps pyproject.toml and CHANGELOG.md.
  4. Review and merge the Release PR when you are ready to ship.
  5. release-please tags vX.Y.Z and publishes the GitHub Release automatically.

Do not manually edit pyproject.toml version for routine releases — release-please owns it.

docs.title: Semver from commits
docs.text:
Commit type Version bump fix: patch feat: minor feat!: or BREAKING CHANGE: footer major

docs:, chore:, test:, and refactor: commits typically do not trigger a release unless they include a recognized release trigger.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text: File Purpose release-please-config.json Release type (python), changelog path .release-please-manifest.json Current released version tracker CHANGELOG.md Human-readable release history

docs.title: First release
docs.text:
The manifest seeds version 1.0.0. After enabling release-please, merge the first Release PR it opens to publish v1.0.0.

The release-as: 1.0.0 setting in release-please-config.json forces the first release version. Remove it after the initial release so later versions follow commit semantics.

docs.title: CI on Release PRs
docs.text: GitHub's default GITHUB_TOKEN may not re-trigger other CI workflows on release-please PRs. For this repository, manually verify Release PRs before merge. If that becomes painful, add a fine-grained PAT as a repository secret and pass it to the workflow token input.

docs.title: Optional announcements
docs.text: For larger features, post a short note in GitHub Discussions (Announcements category) after merging a Release PR. Discussions must be enabled in repository settings.

docs.title: Plugin Catalog
docs.text: The central registry at registry/plugins.yaml indexes all distributable plugins. Each plugin is a self-contained bundle of skills, agents, commands, and optional MCP configs.

docs.title: Install a plugin
docs.text:
agent-foundry install-plugin <provider> <plugin_id>

Example:

agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli git

Install a single skill or agent from a plugin:

agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli git:commit
agent-foundry install agent cursor software-development-agents:senior-ai-engineer

See Installation and CLI reference for all options.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Run agent-foundry --help at any time for the latest option list.

Quick help

Every command below accepts --help. Example: agent-foundry install-plugin --help

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
Flag Description --version Print the installed CLI version and exit. --help Show command help and exit.

When you run a subcommand, agent-foundry may print a one-line update hint if a newer GitHub release exists. See Staying up to date to upgrade or disable the check (AGENT_FOUNDRY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1).

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
All install and uninstall commands require a <provider>:

Provider Description claude Claude Code codex OpenAI Codex copilot GitHub Copilot CLI cursor Cursor IDE cursor-cli Cursor CLI

See Providers and Scope for install-path behavior.

docs.title: Shared flags
docs.text:
These flags apply to install commands (install-plugin, install):

Flag Description --repo PATH_OR_URL Local repository root or git remote URL. Registry checkouts use registry/plugins.yaml; external repos use agents/, skills/, and plugins/ at the root. If omitted, install fetches the default agent-foundry repository first. --global Install to user-level paths (default). --in-project Install relative to the current working directory. --path <kind>:<dir> Repeatable. Override source directories inside the plugin. Kinds: skills, agents, commands, mcp. See Source path overrides. --force Cursor CLI only: overwrite existing agent files in ~/.cursor/agents/ that belong to another install or were not created by agent-foundry.

Uninstall commands accept --repo, --global, and --in-project. Uninstall does not require --path (install state tracks destinations).

docs.title: install-plugin
docs.text:
Install a registry plugin for a provider.

agent-foundry install-plugin <provider> <plugin_id> [options]

Arguments:

  • provider — target tool (see table above)
  • plugin_id — plugin id from the registry, or directory name under plugins/ for external repositories

Examples:

agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli git
agent-foundry install-plugin codex software-development-agents --in-project
agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli my-plugin --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

docs.title: uninstall-plugin
docs.text:
Remove a registry plugin installation for a provider.

agent-foundry uninstall-plugin <provider> <plugin_id> [options]

Use the same --global / --in-project scope as the original install.

Example:

agent-foundry uninstall-plugin codex git --in-project

docs.title: install
docs.text:
Install one specific kind item for a provider.

agent-foundry install <kind> <provider> <identifier> [options]

Arguments:

  • kind — agent, skill, or mcp-config
  • provider — target tool
  • identifier — unique item name; use <plugin_id>:<identifier> when names overlap

Examples:

agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli git:commit --in-project
agent-foundry install agent cursor senior-ai-engineer
agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli commit --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

docs.title: uninstall
docs.text:
Remove one specific kind item for a provider.

agent-foundry uninstall <kind> <provider> <identifier> [options]

Example:

agent-foundry uninstall agent cursor senior-ai-engineer

docs.title: validate-plugins
docs.text:
Validate registry/plugins.yaml and all plugin manifests. Run from the repository root during development.

agent-foundry validate-plugins

No arguments. Exits non-zero if validation fails.

docs.title: create-plugin
docs.text:
Create a new plugin directory and append it to the registry.

agent-foundry create-plugin <plugin_id> [--version VERSION] [--summary "TEXT"]

Arguments:

  • plugin_id — lowercase kebab-case id (e.g. my-plugin)

Options:

  • --version — initial semver (default: 0.1.0)
  • --summary — short description for manifests and registry

Example:

agent-foundry create-plugin my-workflow --version 0.1.0 --summary "My custom workflow plugin"

See Plugin development for layout details.

docs.title: remove-plugin
docs.text:
Drop a plugin from registry/plugins.yaml and delete plugins/<plugin_id>/.

agent-foundry remove-plugin <plugin_id>

This only affects the repository — it does not uninstall from user machines.

Example:

agent-foundry remove-plugin my-workflow

Command Purpose validate-plugins Check registry and manifest consistency create-plugin Scaffold a new plugin remove-plugin Remove a plugin from the registry

docs.title: External Repositories
docs.text: Use --repo to install plugins, agents, or skills from a git remote URL or local directory instead of the default agent-foundry fetch.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
External repositories do not require registry/plugins.yaml. They follow this layout:

repo-root/
  agents/
    senior-reviewer.md
  skills/
    commit/
      SKILL.md
  plugins/
    my-plugin/
      agents/
        plugin-agent.md
      skills/
        plugin-skill/
          SKILL.md

docs.title: Full agent-foundry checkout
docs.text:
When --repo points to a full agent-foundry checkout (with registry/plugins.yaml), plugin lookup uses the registry as usual. This is useful for development or installing from a fork.

Private repositories use your existing git credentials. Ref/tag pinning is not supported yet.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Replace the URL with your repository:

# Standalone skill from repo root
agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli commit --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

# Standalone agent from repo root
agent-foundry install agent cursor-cli senior-reviewer --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

# Full plugin directory under plugins/
agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli my-plugin --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

# Skill inside a plugin (scoped identifier)
agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli my-plugin:plugin-skill --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

# Agent inside a plugin
agent-foundry install agent cursor-cli my-plugin:plugin-agent --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

docs.title: Local path
docs.text:
--repo also accepts a local directory path:

agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli git --repo /path/to/agent-foundry
agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli commit --repo /path/to/my-agents

docs.title: Source path overrides
docs.text: External repos with non-standard directory layouts can use --path to redirect where skills, agents, and other content are read. See Source path overrides.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
agent-foundry is a CLI for installing registry-defined plugins into Codex, Claude Code, Cursor (IDE and CLI), and Copilot CLI.

Plugins live in the repository under plugins/ and are indexed in registry/plugins.yaml. You install bundles (or individual agents, skills, and MCP configs) into the AI tool you use day to day.

What you'll need

Python 3.10+ and pipx. The whole setup takes about two minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+
  • pipx (recommended for installing the CLI)

docs.title: Install the CLI
docs.text:
pipx install git+https://github.com/josemiguelmelo/agent-foundry.git

Verify the install:

agent-foundry --help
agent-foundry --version

docs.title: Install your first plugin
docs.text:
Replace <provider> with your target tool and <plugin_id> with a plugin from the plugin catalog:

agent-foundry install-plugin <provider> <plugin_id>

Example — install the git plugin for Cursor CLI:

agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli git

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This page covers how to install the agent-foundry CLI and how plugin installation resolves its source repository.

docs.title: Install via pipx
docs.text:
The recommended install path uses pipx so the CLI is isolated from your system Python:

pipx install git+https://github.com/josemiguelmelo/agent-foundry.git
agent-foundry --version

To upgrade later or subscribe to release notifications, see Staying up to date.

For local development from a checkout:

pip install -e .
agent-foundry --help

docs.title: Install a plugin
docs.text:
Install or remove a registry plugin for a provider:

agent-foundry install-plugin <provider> <plugin_id>
agent-foundry uninstall-plugin <provider> <plugin_id>

Install or remove a single item (agent, skill, or MCP config):

agent-foundry install <kind> <provider> <identifier>
agent-foundry uninstall <kind> <provider> <identifier>

Replace:

  • <provider> — one of: claude, codex, copilot, cursor, cursor-cli
  • <plugin_id> — a plugin id from the plugin catalog
  • <kind> — one of: agent, skill, mcp-config
  • <identifier> — item name (agent stem, skill folder name, or MCP server id). Use <plugin_id>:<identifier> when names overlap across plugins.

docs.title: Default repository resolution
docs.text: By default, install-plugin tries to fetch the agent-foundry repository from GitHub and resolves plugin paths from that clone. If the fetch fails, it falls back to local registry discovery (useful when developing from a checkout).

docs.title: Install from a custom repository
docs.text:
Pass --repo with a local path or git remote URL (HTTPS/SSH) to install from a custom repository instead of the default fetch:

agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli git --repo /path/to/agent-foundry
agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli commit --repo https://github.com/org/my-agents.git

For a full agent-foundry checkout (with registry/plugins.yaml), --repo uses registry-based plugin lookup. Private repositories use your existing git credentials; ref/tag pinning is not supported yet.

See External repositories for layout requirements and examples.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
By default, installs are global (paths under your home directory). Use --in-project to install into the current working directory instead.

Use the same scope for install and uninstall operations. See Scope for provider-specific behavior.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: agent-foundry supports five provider targets. Each maps plugin content (skills, agents, commands, MCP configs) to the discovery paths expected by that tool.

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text: Provider Tool Notes claude Claude Code Installs under ~/.agent-foundry/... codex OpenAI Codex Project installs use ./.codex/plugins/ copilot GitHub Copilot CLI Project installs mirror into ./.github/skills/, ./.github/agents/, and ./.claude/commands/ cursor Cursor IDE Same project behavior as cursor-cli cursor-cli Cursor CLI Mirrors skills and agents into ~/.cursor/skills/ and ~/.cursor/agents/ (global scope)

docs.title: Cursor CLI behavior
docs.text:
cursor-cli mirrors plugin skills and agents into Cursor CLI discovery paths when using global scope:

  • Skills → ~/.cursor/skills/<skill-name>/
  • Agents → ~/.cursor/agents/<agent-name>.md
  • Install state → ~/.agent-foundry/cursor-cli/

The --force flag is available on Cursor CLI install commands to overwrite agent files that were not created by agent-foundry.

docs.title: Project-local behavior
docs.text: When you pass --in-project, each provider writes to different project paths. See the full table in Scope.

docs.title: Install kinds
docs.text:
For granular installs with install / uninstall, supported kinds are:

Kind Description agent A single agent definition (.md file) skill A single skill directory with SKILL.md mcp-config An MCP server configuration entry

Use <plugin_id>:<identifier> when the same name exists in multiple plugins.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Claude Code
agent-foundry install-plugin claude git

# Codex (project-local)
agent-foundry install-plugin codex git --in-project

# Cursor CLI (global)
agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli software-development-agents

# Copilot CLI
agent-foundry install-plugin copilot project-management

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Install scope controls whether plugin content is written to user-level paths (global) or the current project directory.

Use matching scope

Always uninstall with the same scope you used to install. Mixing --global and --in-project leaves orphaned files.

docs.title: Global vs project-local
docs.text: Scope Flag Root Global (default) --global Your home directory Project-local --in-project Current working directory

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Global install (default)
agent-foundry install-plugin codex git

# Project-local install
agent-foundry install-plugin codex git --in-project

# Remove from project-local scope
agent-foundry uninstall-plugin codex git --in-project

# Install one skill directly into the project
agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli git:commit --in-project

# Remove one agent (global)
agent-foundry uninstall agent cursor senior-ai-engineer

docs.title: Provider behavior with --in-project
docs.text: Provider --in-project behavior cursor Same as cursor-cli: ./.cursor/skills/, ./.cursor/agents/, state under ./.agent-foundry/cursor-cli/. The IDE does not load ./.cursor/plugins/local/ in projects. cursor-cli ./.cursor/ plus state under ./.agent-foundry/cursor-cli/ codex ./.codex/plugins/ and ./.agents/plugins/marketplace.json copilot Mirrors plugin kinds into ./.github/skills/, ./.github/agents/, and ./.claude/commands/ claude No effect — installs stay under ~/.agent-foundry/...

docs.title: When to use each scope
docs.text:
Global (--global):

  • Personal workflows you want available in every project
  • Cursor CLI skills and agents in ~/.cursor/
  • Default for most single-developer setups

Project-local (--in-project):

  • Team-shared agent configs committed alongside the codebase
  • Codex or Copilot project-specific plugin layouts
  • Reproducible setups per repository

docs.title: Source Path Overrides
docs.text:
Use repeatable --path <kind>:<dir> on install-plugin and install to override where skills, agents, commands, or MCP configs are read inside the plugin (manifest source roots).

Paths are relative to the plugin root unless absolute.

docs.title: Supported kinds
docs.text:
Kind Maps to skills Skill directories agents Agent definition files commands Command definitions mcp MCP server configs (mcpServers in manifests)

Uninstall does not require --path — install state tracks the actual destinations.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Registry plugin with a non-default layout:

agent-foundry install-plugin cursor-cli my-plugin \
  --path skills:./vendor/skills \
  --path agents:./vendor/agents

External repo with skills in a custom directory:

agent-foundry install skill cursor-cli commit \
  --repo /path/to/my-agents \
  --path skills:./alt-skills

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
• Plugins that vendor third-party skills or agents in non-standard folders
  • External repositories that do not follow the default skills/ and agents/ layout at the plugin root
  • Migrating existing plugin trees without restructuring directories

docs.title: Staying up to date
docs.text: agent-foundry ships new features and fixes through GitHub Releases. This page explains how to hear about updates and upgrade the CLI.

docs.title: Subscribe to release notifications
docs.text:
The most reliable way to get notified is to watch the repository on GitHub:

  1. Open josemiguelmelo/agent-foundry.
  2. Click Watch → Custom.
  3. Enable Releases only.

You will receive GitHub notifications when a new release is published.

docs.title: Upgrade the CLI
docs.text:
If you installed with pipx (recommended):

pipx upgrade agent-foundry

To install a specific release tag:

pipx install --force git+https://github.com/josemiguelmelo/agent-foundry.git@v1.0.0

Replace v1.0.0 with the version shown on the Releases page.

Check your installed version:

agent-foundry --version

docs.title: CLI update notice
docs.text:
When you run a subcommand, agent-foundry may print a one-line hint on stderr if a newer GitHub release exists. The notice appears at most once per new release version.

Disable the check:

export AGENT_FOUNDRY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1

The check uses the public GitHub API and fails silently when offline or when no releases exist yet.

docs.title: Optional: GitHub Discussions
docs.text: If repository Discussions are enabled, maintainers may post feature announcements in an Announcements category. Subscribe to that category for broader updates beyond release notes.
